questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Love the city and the academics and art scene.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very difficult. There were a lot of deadlines and papers that we needed to fill out and it was super confusing.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was helped with the check in, and later that day we had an orientation dinner.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There were sooo many obligatory meetings about things that did not seem important, and it made things more confusing.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Great options, rooms, single rooms, i had a room in an apartment.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We had to choose one but i choose the lowest possible one. I could also cook in my housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: more info about what to select when applying for housing. Maybe it would be beneficial if they talked to us who have been there before.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was confusing and a long process, but it also involves the process of going to the US.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The website was very confusing, but I would call the different offices all the time as I was super confused. But they answered emails quickly and would try and help over the phone.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I wish we could have registered earlier, because when it opened for us so many students had had access for a while. I had help form our dean, but would have liked more info about the classes before.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Read a lot about the classes and professors but be quick and apply for classes when the deadline opens. Also choose a lot and use the shopping week.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 3 BA and 1 MA. I liked mixing but one of my BA-courses was as difficult as the MA in a good way.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: So many ressources at Barnard and Columbia. Also a lot more was required of the students and at UCPH they dont take attendence and what you in class doesnt count towards your final grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Buoyancy
Intimate Companions - Reading and Writing
Contemporary Latin American Art
Origins of Modern Visual Culture

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Contemporary Latin American Art: great introduction course to non-western art, not super difficult, Madeline Turner is super great
Origins of Modern Visual Culture: A classic art history course but more exciting and with a wonderful professor 
Buoyancy: this was the best class i have ever taken but the teacher stopped at the school after my class

questions.answer: Food was very very expensive.

questions.answer: Going out to eat.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many clubs and events

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Going to the welcome dinners and columbia organized events. Go to the festival!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Museums! There are so many amazing collections. There is also the museum upstate called Dia Beacon. Its a beautiful train ride away from NYC and much calmer.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: In the beginning i felt anxious but we had snowstorms and it got dark very early. After a couple weeks i felt a lot safer.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take smaller classes and talk to them there. Sit in the same spot every class and go on trips if the professor organizes anything

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: socializing. American students are always out doing something so you might not see your roomates ever. And there is a level of superficiality when speaking to new people there

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: peoples openness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Its worth all the preparations and documents
travel for spring break
take exciting classes

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Its expensive to live in NYC
Sign up for classes fast and be pushy about getting in
email everyone

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The classes and the lovely people i met and made friends with

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: getting used to a different academic environment that has more competition

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
